results.question: List out the account numbers of female clients who are oldest and has lowest average salary, calculate the gap between this lowest average salary with the highest average salary?
results.ground_truth_sql: SELECT T1.account_id, (SELECT MAX(A11) - MIN(A11) FROM district) FROM account AS T1 INNER JOIN district AS T2 ON T1.district_id = T2.district_id INNER JOIN disp AS T3 ON T1.account_id = T3.account_id INNER JOIN client AS T4 ON T3.client_id = T4.client_id WHERE T2.district_id = (SELECT district_id FROM client WHERE gender = 'F' ORDER BY birth_date ASC NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1) ORDER BY T2.A11 DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1

WITH female_clients AS (
    SELECT c.client_id, AVG(o.amount) AS avg_salary
    FROM client c
    JOIN disp d ON c.client_id = d.client_id
    JOIN account a ON d.account_id = a.account_id
    JOIN order o ON a.account_id = o.account_id
    WHERE c.gender = 'female'
    GROUP BY c.client_id
),
oldest_female_client AS (
    SELECT client_id, MIN(birth_date) AS min_birth_date
    FROM client
    WHERE gender = 'female'
    GROUP BY client_id
),
oldest_female_client_with_salary AS (
    SELECT fc.client_id, fc.avg_salary
    FROM female_clients fc
    JOIN oldest_female_client ofc ON fc.client_id = ofc.client_id
    WHERE fc.avg_salary = (
        SELECT MIN(avg_salary)
        FROM female_clients
    )
),
highest_avg_salary AS (
    SELECT MAX(avg_salary) AS max_avg_salary
    FROM female_clients
)
SELECT oldest_female_client_with_salary.client_id, oldest_female_client_with_salary.avg_salary, highest_avg_salary.max_avg_salary, (highest_avg_salary.max_avg_salary - oldest_female_client_with_salary.avg_salary) AS salary_gap
FROM oldest_female_client_with_salary, highest_avg_salary;
